GENERAL SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----

   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.

   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and coordination ● Types of nastic responses (haptonasty, chemonasty, t? (1 mark)

   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature? (1 mark)

   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

16. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
